# Large number of Chinese students using AI tools, nationwide survey finds (China Daily)

By ZOU SHUO | chinadaily.com.cn | Updated: 2026-04-26.

## Key findings
- **More than 60 percent** of primary and secondary school students in China have used AI, and **nearly one in five do so regularly**, per a recently released nationwide survey.
- Survey by the **China Youth and Children Research Center**, **June to August last year (2025)**, covered **more than 8,500 students** from **seven regions** (Beijing, Guangdong, Henan, etc.).
- **71 percent** said they use AI to complete homework (searching info, generating ideas). **More than 40 percent** use AI for learning culture and creative purposes (drawing, poetry, posters). **Over 35 percent** chat with AI or share feelings; **about 32 percent** use AI for entertainment.
- 2025: Ministry of Education issued two guidelines promoting scientific/regulated AI use in kindergartens and primary/secondary schools. Tiered approach: primary students not allowed to independently use open-ended generative AI for assignments; middle school students may explore AI-generated content; high school students can do inquiry-based learning on AI technical principles.
- **20.5 percent** said they want to rely on AI for thinking rather than their own minds; **22.8 percent among rural students**.
- **46.4 percent** said they would rather talk to AI than real people when feeling upset; **21 percent** reported anxiety from excessive AI use.
- Sun Hongyan (researcher who led the team): rapid penetration exceeded expectations. "Just a few years ago, less than 20 percent of students had used AI."
- Rural students more likely to use AI for homework/ghostwriting, less likely for creative/innovative purposes. AI could become an "amplifier" of the urban-rural education gap, or a "booster" to narrow it.
- Ning Dan, headmaster of Miaoxi Primary School (rural, Hengyang, Hunan): most students use AI to search answers, chat, make videos, play games; many use grandparents' phones.

## Assessment
- `authoritative: yes` — China Daily is a top-tier state media outlet; English-language report on the same 8,563-student survey (sources 73, 74).
